why: GAP-W1-magic-spellmaking-has-no-world-side-surface, the round-3 verdict's single biggest
gap. `game/data/magic/enchanting.json` names four spellwrights and seven enchanters, and
`game/data/magic/enchant-services.json` prices their shelves, and NONE OF THEM EXISTED AS A
PERSON anywhere in `game/data/npcs/**` — the ids were a foreign key to nobody. So the whole
Morrowind half of the magic piece (a spell you invent, priced, clamped, bought and cast) had
exactly one consumer in the build and it was `window.__HARNESS`. This file is the seven
people. `game/src/sim/magic/commission.js` is the counter they stand behind.
THE SPELLWRIGHT KEY IS THE WIRING. A record's `spellwright` field names a row of
`enchanting.json#spellwrights`; `Engine._commissionOpens()` resolves it and refuses to open a
counter for anybody who has not got one. `enchanter` names a row of `#enchanters` and is
carried for the same reason the ids were authored in the first place — so that the shelf, the
point ceiling and the gold multiplier belong to a PERSON in a PLACE. The enchanting counter
itself is NOT built this round and is declared below.
FOUR MAKE SPELLS AND SEVEN ENCHANT, and the split is the data's own, not a shortcut.
`enchanting.json#spellwright_note` reads: 'Four in the world, and walking to one is part of
the cost (RI-MAG03 A, S7). A single spellwright in the starting town would make spellmaking a
menu and undermine S7's argument that distance is content.' Stormhold, Blackrose and Soulrest
therefore get an ENCHANTER who does not do that work and says who does — which is the same
sentence a Morrowind player gets, and which is what makes the walk content instead of a load
screen. Their `lines.spellmaking` is that refusal, and it names a town.
declared_incomplete: CLOSED IN W1-14 ROUND 5: the enchanting counter is built (`sim/magic/enchant-counter.js`), all seven records open it on the `enchanting` subject, and `enchantQuote` now has a caller that is not the harness. `enchantItem` consumes a filled soul gem and moves the engine's purse, and `useEnchantedItem` spends the object's CHARGE — not Focus — to take hit points off a body, which is the world-side consumer this model had never had. `H.__breakEnchantCounter` leaves the person, the town and the subject and takes the door.

WHAT IS STILL NOT BUILT, said plainly rather than tagged: `on_strike` and `constant` enchantments can be QUOTED and MADE at the counter and are carried in the save, but only `on_use` is consumed — a struck weapon does not fire its enchantment and a worn ring does not apply one, because both need a hook in `combat/resolve.js` and in the equip path that belongs to W1-09 and W1-16 rather than here. A player can therefore make an object this build will not read. The counter says so in the enchanter's own voice before it takes the money.
The four spellwrights keep NO HOURS: their schedule is `at: null` for the whole day, which
`populateSettlement` reads as 'at the authored post'. No interior in this build is a
spellwright's shop, and inventing one would have been a second piece of work hiding inside
this one. A person standing at a post all day is what W1-04's street life already models.

THE TOWN TOPIC WAS REMOVED FROM ALL SEVEN RECORDS. A first draft listed the speaker's own settlement (`lilmoth`, `gideon`, ...) alongside the two service subjects. `topicsFor()` drops a topic the speaker has no info for, so it was never offered to anybody and the probe's topic list showed it absent: a dead entry on the record that reads, to anyone auditing the data, like a subject these people will discuss. They will not. Two subjects each, and both of them answer.

lines.greeting: Slate's wet, ink's wet, everything here is wet. Tell me what it should do and I will tell you what it costs.
lines.enchanting: I put spells into things as well as into people, and the second is cheaper. Seventy points is my ceiling. Above that you want Blackrose or Soulrest, and above THEM you want the Stone Wastes, and you do not want the Stone Wastes.
lines.spellmaking: Slate. Say what it should do, how far it should reach and how hard you want it to bite, and I will price it while you talk.

post.note: On the quay side of the ledger house, and the position is MEASURED rather than chosen: a walk from the town-lilmoth spawn to the scribe's stair aborts `stuck` at 8.5 m of 25.9 and to the smithy at 10.35 m off — there are buildings between the quay and the market side that no walked route in this build gets past, which is a W1-04 world-collision fact and not this piece's. The spellwright stands where a player can actually reach on foot. y is the heightfield at the quay (2.68); Lilmoth's authored posts use 0.37 and 7.37, which are the stilt-town's two deck levels, and a person authored at 0.37 here would be 2.3 m under the street. W1-14 r4.

lines.greeting: You have come up the river to have a thing made that nobody has made. Good. Half of what walks in here wants a spell that already exists.
lines.enchanting: Bring the item, bring the gem, and bring the gem full. I will not fill it for you and neither will anybody honest.
lines.spellmaking: Then we begin at the beginning: what should it do? Not what it should be called. What it should do.

post.note: Beside the apothecary; the two trades share a fire. W1-14 r4.

lines.greeting: Stand where the bole shades you. What you are about to ask for has never been asked for, and that is not a boast, it is arithmetic.
lines.enchanting: The bole takes an enchantment better than a blade does. Seventy points and no further; I have watched a man insist past his ceiling and I have watched what he was holding.
lines.spellmaking: The bole writes better than I do. Tell it what you want and I will hold the chalk.

post.note: Under the hollow bole. W1-14 r4.

npcs.name: Kuleen-Vokh
npcs.title: The recluse of the Stone Wastes

lines.greeting: You found the stair. Most do not. Say the thing you want and say it once; I dislike repetition and I dislike company.
lines.enchanting: A hundred and sixty points. There is nobody else in the province who will say that number to you, which is why you are standing in a hole in the ground having walked four days.
lines.spellmaking: Say it. I will not ask twice and I will not soften the price.

post.note: Not a townsperson. Quest-gated by `mag_recluse_introduction` on the enchanting.json row itself: the counter refuses to open until that flag is set, and the refusal is the gate finally having something behind it. W1-14 r4.

lines.greeting: Rootpost side. Mind the ash; it gets into the settings and then the setting is worth nothing.
lines.spellmaking: I do not write spells. I put them into objects, which is a different trade and a better-paid one. If you want a spell made, that is Lilmoth, or Gideon, or Helstrom. Helstrom is nearest from here and the road is not the worst of them.
lines.enchanting: Seventy points, an item, and a gem with something in it. The gem is your business and I do not ask.

lines.greeting: A prison town is the right town for this work. Nobody here asks where a soul came from.
lines.spellmaking: Writing a spell is a scribe's trade with the wind behind it. I am not a scribe. Gideon has one, and Gideon is four days upriver, and you will find the four days are part of what you are paying.
lines.enchanting: A hundred and ten points, and forty in the hundred over what a journeyman would ask. You are paying for the ceiling, not for the hands.

lines.greeting: The Court counts its dead and I count my points, and only one of those two counts is accurate.
lines.spellmaking: Not my trade. Lilmoth has a spellwright and Lilmoth is downriver of everything, which is the one convenient thing anybody has ever said about Lilmoth.
lines.enchanting: A hundred and ten. Bring the item whole; I will not enchant a thing that is already cracked, whatever you have been told in the market.
